title: Batch Geocoder: 50 Addresses to Coordinates
description: Geocode up to 50 addresses at once, or reverse-geocode coordinate pairs, with the Batch Geocoder — CSV in your spreadsheet's language. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a 50-row mailing list becomes a 50-row coordinate table in one run — the list a map can finally read, exported as CSV.
quick_answer: The Batch Geocoder turns up to 50 pasted addresses into coordinates, or 50 coordinate pairs into addresses, in one rate-limited run, and downloads the results as CSV. Paste one entry per line, choose the direction, run it, and take the table to your spreadsheet, CRM or map.

faq: How many rows can I run?
Up to 50 per batch — paste one entry per line. Bigger lists chunk into fifties; the limit keeps the run inside the geocoding service's fair-use pace.
Rate limiting, deliberately: results arrive at the speed open geocoding politely allows. It is minutes for a full batch, and the alternative (hammering the service) helps nobody's next batch.
Is data uploaded to MapBench servers?
The lookups run against the geocoding service to resolve your lines — that is how geocoding works. MapBench does not keep your list; the CSV you download is your copy.
No — bulk geocoding is not CASS-style postal validation. It places points well; deliverability certification is a separate official process.
Forward vs reverse — which do I need?
Addresses in hand → forward, for coordinates. Coordinates in hand → reverse, for addresses. The names describe what you paste.
One complete address per line (number, street, town, postcode, country where ambiguous) or one 'lat, lng' pair per line for reverse. Completeness is accuracy.
Fix that line's address (more detail usually) and run it singly in Address to Coordinates. Batch failures are per-row, never contagious.
They geocode twice and agree with themselves — harmless but wasteful. Dedupe in the spreadsheet first for a cleaner table.
Include the country in each line and the forward direction handles the mixture; ambiguity, not nationality, is what breaks rows.
